Founder’s Briefs
: An occasional series where Mongabay founder
Rhett Ayers Butler
shares analysis, perspectives and story summaries.
In a quiet corner of northern New York state, the white pines of the Adirondack Forest Preserve rise like sentinels, untouched for more than 125 years. Their silence speaks volumes. These towering trees, some 150 feet (about 46 meters) tall and more than a century old, stand as evidence of a counterintuitive climate solution: do nothing.
Well, not quite nothing. Proforestation, a term coined by academics William Moomaw and Susan Masino in 2019, refers to the practice of leaving existing forests to grow unbothered until they reach their full ecological potential. Unlike reforestation or afforestation, which involve planting new trees, proforestation champions mature forests precisely because of what they already are.
“It’s the existing forests that we have that are doing the work,” Moomaw says.
And quite a bit of work at that: forests annually remove nearly 30% of human-generated CO₂ emissions. The largest 1% of trees by diameter in a mature forest can store half its carbon.
But their value transcends carbon. Old-growth forests are biological fortresses, rich in complexity: downed logs, snags, towering trunks, and diverse canopies. This intricate architecture provides shelter for species that would otherwise vanish, from spotted owls in the Pacific Northwest to elusive salamanders in the mossy understory. Strip away the ancient trees, and you unravel webs of life evolved over centuries.
They are hydrological engineers, too. With deeper roots and broader crowns, old trees drive evapotranspiration, moving water from soil to sky. Cut them down, and landscapes dry out.
As Masino puts it bluntly to
Sruthi Gurudev
, “Nature needs room to breathe. We can’t leave everything open to manipulation and extraction. It’s deadly.”
There is no app to replicate the wisdom encoded in an ancient forest. Genetic diversity, essential for adapting to an unpredictable climate, cannot be replanted wholesale. Nor can the cultural or spiritual gravity of landscapes that predate the internal combustion engine.
Yet old-growth logging persists, a hangover from an era when dominion trumped deference. Of the old forests that once blanketed the U.S., perhaps a tenth remain.
“They are the only survivors of American handiwork,” says ecologist Beverly Law.
Letting forests grow might sound passive, but in the age of climate chaos, patience is an act of radical stewardship.

Beyond reforestation, let’s try ‘proforestation’
” by contributor Sruthi Gurudev for Mongabay.

data.title: Show HN: I built a tool that texts you if your server goes down
data.author: SantiagoVargas
data.article_summary: "YourServerIsDown" 是一个服务器监控服务，帮助企业避免因服务器宕机而流失客户。用户注册后，可在30秒内开始监控服务器，并在服务器出现问题时通过短信即时接收警报，从而快速修复问题，减少销售损失和客户流失。服务覆盖全球多个国家和地区，用户需提供姓名和电话，设置监控的服务器URL。定价为每50次事件4.99美元。该服务承诺简便快捷，确保客户满意。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕服务器宕机监控工具YourServerIsDown.com的实用性、使用场景、以及与其他解决方案的比较。

不同观点：
• SantiagoVargas（开发者）：开发YourServerIsDown.com作为 side project，用于快速检测服务器是否宕机。强调其简单、易于设置，并且避免了Twilio等服务的月费。提供了一个基本的解决方案，适用于不需要深度监控的小型项目或初创公司。

• cocoa19（企业服务视角）：认为该工具不适合大多数企业服务，企业更需要全面的监控系统，如Thousand Eyes，并且通常不希望将健康检查端点暴露给外部，存在安全风险。

• RandomUser4976（特殊使用场景）：分享了其孩子需要持续监控血糖读数的紧急使用场景，认为该服务对其非常有用，能够预防紧急情况。同时询问了如何添加多个监控端点。

• bguebert（类似工具分享）：提到使用Smokeping和vtext.com发送短信的类似解决方案，分享了开源工具的链接。

• based2（比较其他服务）：询问YourServerIsDown.com与Site24x7服务的比较，关注其功能和性价比。

• bitbasher（质疑有效性）：认为这种通知方式容易产生误报，导致浪费时间进行检查。同时提出如果没有用户报告宕机，是否真的算宕机的哲学性问题，表明自己依赖客户反馈来发现问题。

• vivzkestrel（技术细节询问）：询问如何判断服务器是否宕机，关注工具的技术实现细节。

• sam_goody（自托管解决方案）：推荐使用UptimeKuma和Tianji等自托管解决方案，指出这些工具功能更全面，但需要自行设置和托管。

补充讨论：
• 不同用户对监控工具的需求和使用场景存在较大差异，从企业级需求到个人紧急情况，再到小型项目或初创公司。
• 对工具的有效性和误报问题存在争议，部分用户认为简单通知方式不够可靠，更倾向于自托管或深度监控服务。
• 用户对如何扩展工具功能（如添加多个端点）提出了实际使用中的疑问。

data.title: Airbnb will now show total prices by default
data.author: lavabender
data.article_summary: Airbnb将从现在开始在其网站上显示总价格，包括费用和税费，以提高价格透明度。此前，平台仅显示每晚基础价格，额外费用在结账时才显示。此变化是Airbnb致力于“可负担性和透明度”的一部分，也响应了美国联邦贸易委员会即将于5月12日生效的禁止隐藏费用的新规定。自2019年起，Airbnb已在部分国家和地区试行显示总价功能，2022年扩展至加拿大和美国，已有近1700万用户使用该功能。Airbnb表示，该工具帮助降低了房主的清洁费，2023年有近30万房源取消或降低了费用，40%的活跃房源取消了清洁费。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何获取跨国公司产品的价格透明信息

不同观点：
• 第一种观点（SOLAR_FIELDS）：可以通过访问澳大利亚或荷兰的网站来获取那些在其他地区未提供价格透明的全球公司的价格信息。这些国家有法律规定要求公司提供价格透明度。
  - 论据：澳大利亚和荷兰的法律法规强制要求公司在其网站上提供价格透明信息，因此可以通过这些国家的网站获取相关信息。
  - 例子：提到澳大利亚和荷兰的网站作为获取价格信息的途径。

• 第二种观点（隐含观点）：在某些国家，跨国公司可能没有义务提供价格透明信息，导致消费者获取信息的困难。
  - 论据：不同国家的法律要求不同，导致价格透明度在各地不一致。
  - 例子：暗示除澳大利亚和荷兰以外的其他国家可能缺乏这种透明度。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点：跨国公司是否应在全球范围内统一提供价格透明信息，还是只需遵守各国不同的法律要求。
- 其他值得注意的讨论点：消费者如何利用不同国家的法律规定获取必要的信息，以及这种做法是否普遍可行。

43767440.article_content:
Airbnb will now display total prices on its website.
Gabby Jones/Bloomberg/Getty Images
New York
CNN
—
Among the biggest annoyances of booking an Airbnb are the fees, which can jack up the price of the once affordable alternative to hotels. That’s changing Monday with the platform now displaying the total price on default.
All users will now see the full price of a stay, which includes fees and taxes (depending on location), from the get-go. This marks a change from displaying prices based off the nightly rate. The pricing update is part of Airbnb’s commitment to “affordability and transparency,” according to a
blog post
.
Airbnb’s changes come ahead of new US
federal regulations about junk fees
that are set to go
into effect on May 12. The Federal Trade Commission announced new rules late last year banning hotels, ticketing and short-term rental companies from including hidden junk fees in their total.
Rather than consumers getting hit with “convenience” or “service” fees for hotel bookings and concert tickets at checkout, the rule will ensure that pricing information is presented transparently before consumers agree to pay, the agency previously announced.
The final rule does not limit what sellers can charge for a product or service. Instead, it requires businesses to display the total price, including all additional fees, more prominently than other pricing information.
Airbnb began displaying total prices on default in 2019 in several parts of Australia, Canada and Europe. The change rolled out as an option to
Canada and the US in 2022
with nearly 17 million guests having
used the feature since then, the company said.
The company has credited the tool for lowering cleaning fees from hosts. In
2023
, Airbnb said that nearly 300,000 listings removed or lowered their fees after it launched the tool, with 40% of active listings eliminating their cleaning fee.
